official.deadline_central_display: January 8, 2027, 5 p.m. JST (FY2027 2nd recruitment, submission from host institution to JSPS)
official.deadline_note: FY2027 1st recruitment closed September 25, 2026; FY2027 3rd recruitment deadline is June 4, 2027, 5 p.m. JST. Host institutions may set their own internal deadlines more than one month before the JSPS deadline.
official.status_note: FY2027 2nd recruitment is the next open round: application deadline January 8, 2027 (by 5 p.m. JST), results published mid-May 2027, arrival in Japan August 1, 2027 to March 31, 2028, 20 fellowships awarded.
benefits: A round-trip air ticket (based on JSPS's regulations)
Maintenance allowance: JPY362,000 per month for PhD holders; JPY200,000 per month for non-PhD holders at the time research starts in Japan
A settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 (only applicable for Fellows with 3 or more months of tenure)
A research support allowance to cover cooperative research-related expenses, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an eligible country (US, Canada, European Union countries, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Russia), or have been engaged in research continuously for at least three years at a university or research institution in one of those countries

Have obtained a doctoral degree from a foreign graduate school and, as of April 1 of the fiscal year, be within six years of obtaining it, OR be currently enrolled in a doctoral course at a foreign graduate school and expected to receive a PhD within two years from the fellowship start date

Persons who have previously been awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard (P), Short-term (PE), Short-term (PA), Pathway to University positions in Japan (PU)) are not eligible
Not eligible: those holding resident cards with mailing addresses in Japan at the JSPS application deadline; a Japanese citizen who is also a permanent resident of an eligible country
A selected fellow must submit an original doctoral degree certificate or diploma (or the prospect certificate if the degree is not yet obtained) before the fellowship starting date
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution, using the JSPS Electronic Application System (available approximately two months before each application period)
The host institution must verify that the application has been approved by the head of the institution and that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved
The host researcher must be affiliated with a KAKENHI-eligible research institution and be a full-time researcher, and may submit up to three applications
All fields of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences are eligible
documents: FORM1 (Reference): application form for the JSPS Electronic Application System, completed by the host researcher
FORM2: application form completed by the foreign candidate (Short-term version)
Letter of Recommendation (Sample): one-page letter of recommendation from the candidate's recommender, written in English or in Japanese
selection_criteria: Document review by three examiners on a 1-5 scale, taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential
Panel review in which a specified number of applicants are selected in each review section, based on the averaged document review score

Selection policy includes that the fellowship promotes exchange between Japan and North America and Europe, advances both the candidate's and the host's research, and reflects a concrete research plan devised through close host-candidate communication
For pre-doctoral candidates, the research plan should give consideration to honing research skills; conflict-of-interest reviewers are removed from the Review Committee
coverage: Maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month for PhD holders
Maintenance allowance of JPY200,000 per month for candidates who are not PhD holders when research starts in Japan
Round-trip air ticket (based on JSPS regulations)
Settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 for fellows with three or more months of tenure
Research support allowance for cooperative research-related expenses, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
application_method: Confirm citizenship, permanent residency or three-plus years of continuous research in an eligible country (US, Canada, EU, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Russia)
Secure a host researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible Japanese institution willing to apply on your behalf
Check the host institution's internal deadline, which may be more than one month before the JSPS deadline
Complete the Short-term FORM2 and obtain a one-page recommendation letter in English or Japanese
The host researcher submits FORM1 through the JSPS Electronic Application System and the institution transmits the application to JSPS
official.application_route: A Japanese host researcher applies on the candidate's behalf through the JSPS Electronic Application System and the host institution transmits it to JSPS by the deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an eligible country (US, Canada, European Union countries, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Russia), or have conducted research continuously for at least three years at a university or research institution in one of those countries; persons with resident cards with mailing addresses in Japan at the application deadline are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Open only to overseas researchers based in eligible North American and European countries; researchers already resident in Japan at the deadline are excluded.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction: all fields of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences are eligible.
official.research_requirement: Candidates conduct collaborative research under the guidance of a Japanese host; for pre-doctoral candidates the research plan should give consideration to honing research skills.
official.description: The programme provides PhD students and PhD researchers in Europe and North America with opportunities to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of their hosts in universities and other Japanese institutions for one to twelve months. Financial support comprises a maintenance allowance, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance for longer tenures, overseas travel insurance and a research support allowance for cooperative research-related expenses.
official.program_type: Government research fellowship (JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan, Short-term (PE))

verification.notes: Stipend amounts, financial-support terms, eligibility bars, FY2027 deadlines (Jan 8 2027 and Jun 4 2027 rounds) and required forms verified directly on jsps.go.jp; the site publishes no English test requirement and no tuition provision.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a host-driven award: you cannot apply yourself, so first persuade a full-time researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible Japanese institution to sponsor you through the JSPS Electronic Application System, which opens only about two months before each round. PhD holders receive JPY362,000 per month plus round-trip airfare, a JPY200,000 settling-in allowance for stays of three months or more, and overseas travel insurance, while non-PhD holders start at JPY200,000 per month; there is no tuition support, so budget for your own visa, relocation and research costs. Previous holders of JSPS Standard (P), Short-term (PE/PA) or Pathway (PU) fellowships are barred, and anyone holding a Japanese resident card at the deadline is ineligible.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Researchers from the US, Canada, EU, UK, Switzerland, Norway or Russia within six years of their PhD (or finishing a PhD within two years) who have not previously researched in Japan and can line up a Japanese host.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify and secure a full-time host researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution willing to file the application on your behalf
Ask the host institution for its internal deadline, which can fall more than a month before the JSPS date
Prepare the Short-term FORM2 and a one-page recommendation letter in English or Japanese
Confirm you hold no prior JSPS fellowship under Standard (P), Short-term (PE/PA) or Pathway (PU), and no Japanese resident card at the deadline
If not yet doctored, arrange a prospect certificate; selected fellows must submit the original degree certificate or diploma before the start date
common_rejection_risks: No willing host: the application is submitted by the Japanese host institution, so without a sponsoring researcher there is no application at all
Missing the host institution's internal deadline, which precedes the JSPS deadline by weeks
Weak evidence of a concrete, jointly devised research plan, since the selection policy explicitly rewards close host-candidate communication
Falling outside the six-year window since the PhD, measured as of April 1 of the fiscal year
A prior JSPS fellowship or a Japanese mailing address at the deadline, both automatic bars
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa fees, relocation and shipping, housing deposits beyond the settling-in allowance, and any tuition or bench fees, none of which this stipend-based fellowship covers.
document_audit: FORM2 must be the current short-term version, and the recommendation letter must fit on one page in English or Japanese
The host files FORM1 in the JSPS electronic system roughly two months before each round, so a late host commitment compresses the whole timeline
Degree evidence is required before the fellowship start date (original certificate or diploma, or prospect certificate if not yet obtained), not at application
alerts: Three FY2027 rounds (Sep 25 2026, Jan 8 2027, Jun 4 2027, 20 fellowships each) but the electronic system opens only about two months before each
Outbound airfare and the settling-in allowance are withheld from candidates already living in Japan with a mailing address
Non-PhD holders are paid JPY200,000 per month rather than JPY362,000 from the start of research in Japan
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Host researcher completes FORM1 in the JSPS Electronic Application System, the institution verifies approval and transmits the application to JSPS by the deadline; award letters then go to host institutions.

official.deadline_central_display: 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time (extended deadline for candidate submission)
official.deadline_note: Candidates must submit to their National Commission for UNESCO at least 2 weeks before the deadline; the Application Guide originally listed 30 September 2026 and the programme page (last updated 28 September 2026) extended it to 15 October 2026. Each invited Member State or Associate Member may submit a maximum of two candidates, of whom at least one should be a woman.
official.status_note: The programme page (last updated 28 September 2026) states that the application for the Cycle 2026 is open and that the deadline for candidate submission is now extended to 15 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The grant does not cover tuition fees, the purchase of equipment including computers, publication costs or participation in conferences, unless such participation can be clearly justified as an integral part of the research and makes a direct and significant contribution to the project.
benefits: Fellowship grant of up to US$10,000 provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan

Medical insurance arranged by UNESCO on the fellow's behalf, with the cost deducted from the total fellowship amount before disbursement (indicatively about US$75 per month, US$225-675 in total depending on duration)
Research stay in a Japanese university or research institution from February 2027 onwards, to be completed no later than December 2027
eligibility: Be a national of one of the invited Member States or Associate Members listed in Annex 1 for Cycle 2026
Be no more than 40 years old at the time of application
Hold at least a Master's degree or equivalent in a field relevant to the proposed research and demonstrate strong academic and research potential
Demonstrate sufficient proficiency in reading and writing in the language of instruction or supervision at the proposed host institution in Japan
Have obtained acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution, who will oversee the proposed research
requirements: Submit the application to the National Commission for UNESCO of your home country at least 2 weeks before the required deadline; only applications nominated by the National Commission will be accepted by UNESCO
Once nominated, communicate the online application form and supporting documents to keizoobuchi.fellowships@unesco.org no later than 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time
The research proposal must fall within one of the five listed research areas, selecting one primary research area and one corresponding sub-area from Annex 2
Each invited Member State or Associate Member may submit a maximum of two candidates, of whom at least one should be a woman
documents: Fellowship application form (Annex 3), duly completed in English or French

Academic documents: certified copies of diplomas (or official proof of student status for prospective diploma winners) and academic transcripts, with notarized English or French translations for documents in other languages
Letter of recommendation from a referee familiar with the candidate's research or professional work
Letter of acceptance from the host institution, indicating willingness to receive the candidate and provide the necessary supervision and research facilities in the proposed field of study

Certificate of language proficiency (such as IELTS, TOEFL or JLPT where applicable), or the UNESCO Certificate of Language Knowledge (Annex 5), duly completed, signed and stamped by a certified language institution or language tutor
Research proposal (Annex 4 template, English or French, maximum 3 pages) including a budget expressed in US dollars not exceeding US$10,000
selection_criteria: Evaluation by a Selection Committee composed of experts from UNESCO and the Government of Japan in the relevant fields
The merits of the candidates and the quality, relevance and originality of the proposed research
The final selection decision is made by the Japanese authorities based on the Committee's recommendation, with due consideration to gender equality and diversity
Candidates who have not been notified of the outcome by 31 January 2027 should consider their application unsuccessful
coverage: International and domestic travel for the approved itinerary
Medical insurance (deducted from the total fellowship amount before disbursement)
Personal subsistence in Japan, including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses
Not covered: tuition fees, purchase of equipment including computers, publication costs, or participation in conferences unless clearly justified as an integral part of the research
application_method: Read carefully the Cycle 2026 Application Guide
Contact the National Commission for UNESCO of your home country to enquire about the procedures and any pre-selection at national level
Obtain acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution
Prepare the application form (Annex 3), academic documents, recommendation letter, host institution acceptance letter, language certificate and research proposal (Annex 4)

Submit the application to your National Commission at least 2 weeks before the deadline; once nominated, send the online application form and supporting documents to keizoobuchi.fellowships@unesco.org
official.application_route: Apply through your National Commission for UNESCO; only Commission-nominated applications are accepted by UNESCO, which receives them at keizoobuchi.fellowships@unesco.org.
official.citizenship_residency: Be a national of one of the invited Member States or Associate Members listed in Annex 1 for Cycle 2026: 47 African Member States; Bahrain; 17 Asia and the Pacific Member States plus 2 Associate Members; 16 Latin America and the Caribbean Member States plus 7 Associate Members; and Ukraine and Türkiye.
official.international_eligibility: Open to nationals of the invited Member States and Associate Members only; research is carried out in Japan under the supervision of a Japanese academic host.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The proposal must fall within one of five research areas: Heritage Conservation and Management; AI for Sustainable Management of Natural Resources and Climate Action; Ethical, Inclusive and Human-Centred AI for Sustainable Development; AI for Sustainable Cities, Infrastructure and Societal Resilience; or AI and Education.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal (Annex 4 template, English or French, maximum 3 pages) located in one primary research area and one corresponding Annex 2 sub-area, with a realistic budget in USD of no more than US$10,000; the fellowship duration must be no less than 3 months and no more than 9 months.
official.duration: No less than 3 months and no more than 9 months
official.description: Established in 2001 under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust for the Capacity-Building of Human Resources, the UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme enables young researchers to pursue postgraduate research through stays in Japanese universities and research institutions. Under Cycle 2026, 10 fellows receive a lump-sum grant of up to US$10,000 for research related to heritage conservation and management, sustainable development and artificial intelligence.
official.program_type: UN agency research fellowship co-sponsored by the Government of Japan
official.english_requirement: Applicants must demonstrate sufficient proficiency in reading and writing in the language of instruction or supervision at the proposed host institution; proof may be an official language certificate such as IELTS, TOEFL or JLPT where applicable, or otherwise the UNESCO Certificate of Language Knowledge (Annex 5).

verification.notes: US$10,000 ceiling, eligible and excluded costs, insurance deduction (about US$75 per month), document list, nomination rules and selection process confirmed on the UNESCO programme page (updated 28 September 2026) and the Cycle 2026 Application Guide; the extension to 15 October 2026 is published on the programme page and supersedes the 30 September date in the guide.

applicant_utility.summary: Your National Commission for UNESCO is the real gatekeeper: each invited country may nominate at most two candidates, at least one of them a woman, so deliver your file to the Commission by early October even though UNESCO's extended deadline is 15 October 2026 midnight Paris time. The award is a capped lump sum of up to US$10,000, not a salary: it must stretch over airfare, accommodation, meals, local transport and mandatory insurance (about US$75 a month, deducted before you receive the balance), and it explicitly excludes tuition, equipment, publication and conference costs. Come with a Japanese supervisor's acceptance letter and a three-page proposal mapped to one of the five AI or heritage research areas, or the file will not reach the selection committee.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Researchers aged 40 or under from an invited African, Small Island Developing State, Ukrainian or Turkish university who hold at least a Master's, already have a Japanese academic host, and want a 3-9 month research stay in Japan.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact your National Commission for UNESCO immediately to confirm its internal cut-off and any national pre-selection
Obtain the host institution's acceptance letter confirming supervision and research facilities before assembling the file
Draft the Annex 4 proposal to three pages maximum with a USD budget under US$10,000 and one Annex 2 sub-area
Secure a language certificate (IELTS, TOEFL, JLPT) or have the Annex 5 certificate signed and stamped by a certified language institution or tutor
Arrange notarized English or French translations for any diplomas or transcripts issued in another language
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to UNESCO rather than through the National Commission, since only nominated applications are accepted
Missing the Commission's national cut-off, typically two weeks before the 15 October 2026 deadline
Incomplete files: a missing acceptance letter, language proof or budget is grounds for non-consideration
A proposal that does not select one primary Annex 2 research area and sub-area, or a duration outside the 3-9 month window
Assuming the full US$10,000 is spendable, when insurance and ineligible cost lines shrink the usable budget
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, equipment such as laptops, publication and conference costs, plus anything above the US$10,000 ceiling; personal travel or extras beyond the approved itinerary are not eligible.
document_audit: The application form must use the official Annex 3 template in English or French
Certified diploma copies or proof of student status need notarized translations if not in English or French
The proposal budget must be in USD and within the ceiling, with medical insurance cost (about US$225-675) coming off the top before disbursement
The recommendation letter must come from a referee familiar with your research or professional work, not a generic academic contact
alerts: The deadline was extended from 30 September to 15 October 2026 midnight Paris time, but your National Commission still needs at least two weeks
Each country may nominate at most two candidates, at least one woman, so national competition can be tighter than the 10-fellowship quota
If you have not been notified of the outcome by 31 January 2027, treat the application as unsuccessful
Fellows must file interim and final reports and acknowledge UNESCO and the Government of Japan in resulting publications
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: File goes to your National Commission for UNESCO; once nominated, you email the online application form and supporting documents to keizoobuchi.fellowships@unesco.org, which collects nomination letters and documents from the Commissions.
